Hi Sara / Alan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

Summary from today (high level)
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Private (VPC + optional on-prem/air-gapped) as a replacement for current hyperscaler-managed inference endpoints for PHI workloads.
- Primary concerns you raised: private control plane access, networking topology (VPC peering / AWS Transit), egress controls, and air-gap feasibility for offline inference in a regulated environment.

How Redwood differentiates vs hyperscalers we discussed
- Private control plane option: control plane traffic can be restricted to AcmeHealth-managed subnets or deployed as a customer-controlled control plane (no outbound management traffic required for air-gapped mode).
- Predictable throughput vs utility endpoints: Dedicated GPU pools for consistent p50/p99 latency under commit. Hyperscalers often have variable throttling during burst loads.
- Cost controls & insights: token-level cost breakdown + batching/caching recommendations to reduce unit cost — hyperscalers often bill egress + request without per-token tooling.
- Security: native KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2 artifacts, and audit logs included; we can run with customer-managed keys.

Requested next tests (from you) — proposed approach
1) Networking validation: VPC peering / Transit setup + specific firewall/NAT / egress rules validation. We’ll provide a networking checklist and short runbook.
2) Private control plane reachability: test a private endpoint over a site-to-site VPN or AWS PrivateLink; objective is zero-control-plane egress for management operations.
3) Air-gap feasibility: outline of on-prem package and a small air-gapped PoC (bring your images + deploy runtime); will need list of required outbound artifacts and a packaging checklist.

Action items
- Redwood: share networking checklist, SOC2 summary, and a proposed mutual action plan with timelines (assigned: Vanessa / Marissa).
- Acme: confirm network contact for test (we asked for a networking lead + sandbox AWS account or VPC details) and security contact for KMS/HSM questions.
- Schedule: propose a 2-hour networking lab next week to validate peering + NAT config.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short networking checklist and our SOC2 summary for your security team to review.

If that aligns, can you share the best network contact and a couple of available windows for the lab?

Thanks,

Hi Sara / Alan — Vanessa here, looping in Marissa and Camila. Thanks for the clear questions — answers below and next steps. 

Private control plane — short answer
- We support two deployment patterns for control plane management:
  1) Managed-but-private: control plane is hosted by Redwood but connectivity is over PrivateLink / customer VPC peering only (no public internet egress required). All management calls are routed over the PrivateLink endpoint and authenticated via mutual TLS and customer-managed IAM roles.
  2) Customer-hosted control plane: for air-gapped/regulatory customers we provide a customer-deployed control plane image that runs inside your VPC or on-prem. In that mode there is zero control-plane egress — all operations are local to your environment.

Air-gap package — short answer
- The air-gap PoC is fully offline by default: we provide a downloadable bundle (images + installer + offline license) that your infra team deploys behind your firewall. No periodic call-home is required for runtime. Optional metrics/telemetry can be enabled through an approved outbound proxy if you later choose to allow it.

Competitor differentiation (why this is different from hyperscaler proposals)
- Hyperscalers often keep control plane services centralized for patching/management which means occasional outbound management traffic and less visibility into the control plane itself.
- Redwood’s customer-hosted control plane option gives you the same inference runtime we use but under your network and KMS controls; you retain responsibility for control plane lifecycle, avoiding the centralized call-home model.
- We include a SOC2 summary and audit logs appropriate for your security review (attached).

Proposed next steps / lab plan
1) Networking lab (2 hours) — validate PrivateLink + NAT/SG settings in your sandbox VPC. We’ll need a network owner and an IAM role with the following minimal permissions (I’ll attach a pre-check list).
2) Control plane reachability test (30–60 minutes) — validate a PrivateLink endpoint to Redwood-managed control plane, then test the customer-hosted control plane flow in a separate session.
3) Air-gap PoC kickoff (estimate) — 2–3 weeks for packaging and scheduling; 1–2 weeks for deploy & smoke tests in your environment. We’ll provide detailed artifact lists.

Scheduling & resources
